questions.stem: Keystone must serve accounts to five product teams and several agentic apps. One team asks for direct read access to the accounts tables 'for performance'. What do you propose?
options: Grant SELECT on the tables to their role
Keep table ownership in accounts-svc; offer a read API or a GraphQL read layer, and publish change events they can project locally if they need low latency
Copy the tables nightly into their schema
Merge their service into accounts-svc
questions.explanation: Direct table access makes the schema a cross-team contract and bypasses tenancy logic. An API plus events gives them speed without coupling.

questions.stem: The interviewer asks how Keystone isolates tenants that are business units with very different sizes (bu-amer is 20x bu-apac). Choose TWO sound points.
options: Shared schema with RLS by default, with the option to move a very large tenant to its own database later
Per-tenant quotas and rate limits at the API layer to contain noisy neighbors
Create one schema per tenant and run migrations by hand
Disable RLS for the largest tenant for speed
Put all tenants in separate Kubernetes clusters from day one
questions.explanation: Start simple and keep a migration path for an outlier; enforce fairness with quotas. Disabling RLS or hand-run per-schema migrations trade safety for nothing.

questions.stem: Under PgBouncer transaction pooling, a developer sets the tenant with SET app.tenant_id = 'bu-amer' right after checking out a connection, outside any transaction. A bu-emea user later sees bu-amer rows. Why?
options: RLS does not work with PgBouncer
The session-level SET persisted on the server connection, which PgBouncer then handed to another client
current_setting caches across databases
FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY was missing
questions.explanation: Transaction pooling reassigns server connections between transactions, carrying session state. SET LOCAL inside the transaction is the fix.

questions.stem: A query WHERE account_id::text = $1 on a uuid column started doing a sequential scan after a release. The index on account_id exists. Why?
options: The index needs REINDEX
Casting the indexed column means the index (on the uuid value) cannot be used; compare against a uuid parameter instead
ANALYZE was not run
uuid columns cannot be indexed
questions.explanation: An expression on the column defeats a plain index. Cast the parameter, not the column, or build an expression index if you truly need it.

questions.stem: A plan shows Nested Loop (rows=3) (actual rows=410000) with an inner index scan executed 410,000 times. What do you look at first?
options: The server's CPU model
The row estimate error on the outer side: fix statistics (ANALYZE, extended statistics for correlated columns) so the planner can pick a hash join
Disable nested loops globally
Add more indexes until it changes
questions.explanation: Bad estimates drive bad join choices. Fix the estimate rather than forcing planner settings.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Serializable isolation in PostgreSQL are true?
options: It can abort transactions with a serialization failure, so the application must retry
It prevents anomalies such as write skew that Read Committed allows
It takes table locks for every read
It makes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE unnecessary in all cases and has no cost
It is the default isolation level
questions.explanation: SSI detects dangerous patterns and aborts one transaction; you must retry. Read Committed is the default.

questions.stem: accounts-svc uses asyncio.gather to call three partner APIs per request. One hangs for 90 s. What should the code have?
options: Nothing; gather times out by default
A timeout per call (asyncio.timeout or client timeouts) and bounded concurrency, with a clear error mapping
A thread per call
A longer Uvicorn keep-alive
questions.explanation: Every external call needs a deadline. gather waits for the slowest call forever otherwise.

questions.stem: Lazy loading of account.contacts inside an async endpoint raises an error with SQLAlchemy's AsyncSession. What is the idiomatic fix?
options: Switch back to a sync engine
Load eagerly in the query (selectinload) or use explicit awaitable access, avoiding implicit IO on attribute access
Catch and ignore the error
Increase the pool size
questions.explanation: Implicit lazy loads do IO on attribute access, which asyncio cannot do transparently. Eager loading also avoids the N+1.

questions.stem: A client sends POST /v1/accounts with Idempotency-Key K. The first request is still running when an identical retry arrives. What should the second request get?
options: A second account
A 409 Conflict problem response (optionally with Retry-After) because the key is in progress
A 200 with an empty body
It should block for up to 10 minutes
questions.explanation: The key is claimed but has no stored response yet. Reject concurrent use; the client retries and later gets the replayed response.

questions.stem: A partner reports missing contacts while paging. The cursor is the last row's created_at, and the query is WHERE created_at > $cursor ORDER BY created_at. What is the bug?
options: The page size is too small
Rows with identical created_at (from a bulk import) are skipped; the sort and cursor need a unique tie-breaker such as (created_at, id)
Cursors must be integers
The partner should use OFFSET
questions.explanation: Non-unique sort keys make keyset pagination skip or repeat rows at page boundaries. Add the id to both the ORDER BY and the cursor.

questions.stem: A DataLoader is created at module scope in pipeline-svc's GraphQL server. Two weeks later a bu-emea manager sees a bu-amer account name. Why?
options: DataLoader has a bug
The loader cache is shared across requests, so values loaded under one user's authorization are served to another; loaders must be created per request
GraphQL leaks data by design
The CDN cached the response
questions.explanation: Per-request loaders scope the cache and authorization context to the request.

questions.stem: pipeline-svc loses about 0.5% of requests during every rollout. Pods exit within 100 ms of SIGTERM. What is missing?
options: More replicas
Graceful shutdown: stop accepting, wait for endpoint removal (preStop or readiness failure), drain in-flight requests with fastify.close(), then exit
A bigger node
HTTP/2
questions.explanation: Endpoint removal lags the SIGTERM. Draining and a short delay before closing listeners avoid dropped requests.

questions.stem: Consumers see duplicate OpportunityStageChanged events with different event_ids after relay restarts. What is the most likely relay bug?
options: Kafka duplicated them
The relay generates a new event id at publish time instead of reusing the outbox row's id, so consumer dedupe cannot recognize redeliveries
The consumer group rebalanced
The topic has too many partitions
questions.explanation: Redelivery is expected; changing identity is the bug. Keep the outbox row's event_id end to end.

questions.stem: Kafka's idempotent producer is enabled. Which TWO statements are true?
options: It prevents duplicates caused by producer retries within a producer session
It does not make consumers idempotent or remove duplicates from an outbox relay re-reading rows after a crash
It provides exactly-once processing end to end automatically
It guarantees ordering across partitions
It removes the need for an outbox
questions.explanation: Producer idempotence handles broker-level retry duplicates only. Application-level redelivery still needs stable ids and idempotent consumers.

questions.stem: A Go consumer launches one goroutine per message with no limit. During a backlog of 2M messages memory explodes. What is the fix?
options: Add GOGC=off
Bound concurrency with a worker pool or semaphore, and keep per-key ordering by routing a key to one worker
Use channels of size 2M
Rewrite in Java
questions.explanation: Unbounded goroutines are cheap until they are not. A bounded pool applies backpressure; per-key routing preserves ordering.

questions.stem: A Go service uses http.Get to call the accounts API. During an outage of that API every handler hangs. Why?
options: http.Get retries forever
The default http.Client has no timeout; use a client with Timeout and pass request contexts with deadlines
Go cannot do HTTP
The DNS cache is full
questions.explanation: The default client never times out. Always set timeouts and propagate context.

questions.stem: After a deploy, Temporal workers log nondeterminism errors for in-flight lead workflows only; new ones work. What changed?
options: The Temporal server was upgraded
The workflow code changed its command sequence (for example a new activity or datetime.now()) without patching, so old histories no longer replay
The activities got slower
The task queue filled up
questions.explanation: Only replays of old histories fail. Fix with workflow.patched or worker versioning, and add a replay test to CI.

questions.stem: Which statement about Temporal activities is correct?
options: Activities run exactly once
Activities are retried per their retry policy and can run more than once, so side effects need idempotency
Activities must be deterministic
Activities cannot call databases
questions.explanation: At-least-once execution means idempotency keys on external writes.

questions.stem: The import shows 2,000 Accounts in the Salesforce export but 1,987 in Keystone, with some Contacts on the wrong account. IDs were normalized with lower(). What happened?
options: 13 accounts failed validation
Case-distinct 15-character IDs collapsed into the same key, so upserts merged different accounts; convert to 18-character IDs and compare exactly
The CSV had a BOM
Bulk API truncated the export
questions.explanation: 15-character IDs are case-sensitive. Lowercasing merges distinct records; the reconciliation counts exposed it.

questions.stem: During the strangler migration, both Salesforce and Keystone accept edits to Contacts for two weeks. What must exist?
options: Nothing; last write wins is fine
Conflict rules, a sync direction per field, drift detection with reconciliation, and a rollback plan
A freeze on edits
Daily CSV exports
questions.explanation: Dual-write or bidirectional sync needs explicit conflict handling and reconciliation. Prefer one-way CDC with a clear source of truth per phase.

questions.stem: A product team wants their agent to call Keystone with a service account that can read all tenants 'to keep it simple'. What is the problem?
options: Service accounts cannot call MCP servers
The agent would be able to do more than the user it acts for; any injection becomes a cross-tenant breach. Use delegation so the agent acts with the user's identity
It is slower
RLS does not support service accounts
questions.explanation: The agent never gets a broader role than the human. Delegated identity plus RLS makes that hold in the database.

questions.stem: Which TWO controls should hold even if the model is fully compromised by an injected instruction?
options: Tenant scoping derived from the authenticated session
Write tools that only propose and require approval through a workflow
A system prompt saying 'never reveal other tenants'
Lower temperature
A longer tool description
questions.explanation: Server-side scope and approval gates do not depend on model behavior. Prompt text and sampling settings do.

questions.stem: A Helm upgrade adds a NOT NULL column that the new code requires. Old pods still run during the rollout. What is the safe sequence?
options: Add the column as NOT NULL with no default in a pre-upgrade job
Add it nullable (or with a default), deploy code that writes it, backfill, then add NOT NULL (via a validated CHECK) in a later release
Deploy code first, then the migration
Stop all pods during the upgrade
questions.explanation: Expand/contract keeps old and new code compatible at every step of a rolling deploy.

questions.stem: Order a migration of the pipeline capability off the CRM.
options: Decommission the Salesforce pipeline after a rollback window
Inventory objects, fields, validation rules and flows
Delete the Salesforce org first
Route the pipeline app to Keystone and flip the source of truth
Build Keystone pipeline with legacy IDs and a one-way CDC sync from Salesforce
Run reconciliation until counts, checksums and sampled diffs match
questions.explanation: Inventory, build and sync, reconcile, flip, then retire after the rollback window. Each step is reversible until the last.
